Final Cohort Definition

1. Index event
   1.1 Definition: The index date is the calendar date of the later (i.e., second) qualifying condition occurrence when both diagnoses (influenza and constipation) have been observed for the same person within the 2020 calendar year. If both qualifying condition occurrences happen on the same date, that date is the index date.
   1.2 Index event type: Person-level single date (no time) determined as above.

2. Entry criteria (all must be satisfied)
   2.1 Observation period: The person must have at least one condition occurrence of influenza (see Assumptions for concept selection) with event date on or between 2020-01-01 and 2020-12-31 inclusive.
   2.2 Observation period: The person must have at least one condition occurrence of constipation (see Assumptions for concept selection) with event date on or between 2020-01-01 and 2020-12-31 inclusive.
   2.3 Sex: The person’s recorded sex must be male on or before the index date.
   2.4 Age: The person’s age at the index date must be between 20 and 25 years inclusive (i.e., age >= 20 and <= 25 on the index date).

3. Population constraints and deduplication
   3.1 One entry per person: Each person may enter the cohort at most once. If multiple index dates would be generated (e.g., multiple pairs of qualifying events), use the earliest index date in 2020 for that person (i.e., earliest date on which the person first has both conditions present in 2020).
   3.2 Person-level distinctness: Cohort count should be the number of distinct persons meeting the criteria.

4. Visit/setting
   4.1 No restriction on care setting: Qualifying condition occurrences may be recorded in any care setting (inpatient, outpatient, emergency, primary care, etc.).
   4.2 No requirement for same encounter: The influenza and constipation occurrences do not need to be on the same encounter or same visit, only both must occur in 2020 for the same person.

5. Time window
   5.1 Study time window: All qualifying events must occur within the 2020 calendar year (2020-01-01 through 2020-12-31 inclusive).
   5.2 Index date determination reiterated: Index date = date of the later of the two qualifying condition occurrences within this 2020 window.

6. Exclusions
   6.1 No additional clinical exclusions: Do not exclude persons for prior history of either condition outside 2020, nor exclude for missing other demographic data, unless the data necessary to evaluate sex or age are missing (see Assumptions).
   6.2 No visit-type exclusions.

7. Exit
   7.1 Cohort exit date: Each person exits the cohort on the index date (i.e., cohort era length = 0 days). This collection is intended for a cross-sectional/count metric on that index date.

8. Assumptions (explicit, conservative defaults)
   8.1 Condition concept sets: “Influenza” is any condition concept that represents influenza (all acute influenza SNOMED/ICD concepts and their descendants). “Constipation” is any condition concept that represents constipation (and descendants). Implementation in ATLAS should include appropriate standard concept(s) and descendants for each clinical concept. If multiple related subtypes exist (e.g., influenza A/B), include all influenza subtypes.
   8.2 Age calculation: Age is computed using the person’s birth date and the index date using full date precision. If only year of birth is available in the source, compute age conservatively using (index year - birth year) and include patients if the result falls between 20 and 25 inclusive. If birth date is missing such that age cannot be determined, exclude the person (Assumption: require determinable age).
   8.3 Sex definition: “Male” is defined by the recorded sex concept indicating male. If sex is missing or recorded as unknown, exclude the person (Assumption: require determinable recorded sex).
   8.4 Event timing: Only condition occurrences with event dates within 2020-01-01 to 2020-12-31 are allowed to qualify. Condition occurrences before or after 2020 do not satisfy the requirement for that condition.
   8.5 Multiple events: If a person has multiple occurrences of influenza and/or constipation in 2020, use dates as described to determine the index date (the later of one influenza and one constipation event). For per-person deduplication, use the earliest such index date in 2020.
   8.6 Observation continuity: Continuous observation time is not required. Persons without continuous observation are eligible provided qualifying events and demographic data are present in the data.

9. Output/metric
   9.1 Metric requested: Provide the patient count (number of unique persons) meeting the cohort definition above in 2020.

),

  -- all combinations of influenza and constipation events per person within 2020
  SELECT
    i.person_id,
    GREATEST(i.event_date, c.event_date) AS index_date
  FROM influenza_events i
  JOIN constipation_events c

),

  -- choose earliest index date per person

   2.3 Sex: The person’s recorded sex must be male on or before the index date.
   2.4 Age: The person’s age at the index date must be between 20 and 25 years inclusive (i.e., age >= 20 and <= 25 on the index date).

3. Population constraints and deduplication
   3.1 One entry per person: Each person may enter the cohort at most once.    3.2 Person-level distinctness: Cohort count should be the number of distinct persons meeting the criteria.

4. Visit/setting
   4.1 No restriction on care setting: Qualifying condition occurrences may be recorded in any care setting (inpatient, outpatient, emergency, primary care, etc.).
   4.2 No requirement for same encounter: The influenza and constipation occurrences do not need to be on the same encounter or same visit, only both must occur in 2020 for the same person.

5. Time window
   5.1 Study time window: All qualifying events must occur within the 2020 calendar year (2020-01-01 through 2020-12-31 inclusive).
   5.2 Index date determination reiterated: Index date = date of the later of the two qualifying condition occurrences within this 2020 window.

   6.1 No additional clinical exclusions: Do not exclude persons for prior history of either condition outside 2020, nor exclude for missing other demographic data, unless the data necessary to evaluate sex or age are missing (see Assumptions).

{"value": "Final Cohort Definition

1. Index event
   1.1 Definition: The index date is the calendar date of the later (i.e., second) qualifying condition occurrence when both diagnoses (influenza and constipation) have been observed for the same person within the 2020 calendar year. If both qualifying condition occurrences happen on the same date, that date is the index date.
   1.2 Index event type: Person-level single date (no time) determined as above.

2. Entry criteria (all must be satisfied)
   2.1 Observation period: The person must have at least one condition occurrence of influenza (see Assumptions for concept selection) with event date on or between 2020-01-01 and 2020-12-31 inclusive.
   2.2 Observation period: The person must have at least one condition occurrence of constipation (see Assumptions for concept selection) with event date on or between 2020-01-01 and 2020-12-31 inclusive.
   2.3 Sex: The person’s recorded sex must be male on or before the index date.
   2.4 Age: The person’s age at the index date must be between 20 and 25 years inclusive (i.e., age >= 20 and <= 25 on the index date).

3. Population constraints and deduplication
   3.1 One entry per person: Each person may enter the cohort at most once. If multiple index dates would be generated (e.g., multiple pairs of qualifying events), use the earliest index date in 2020 for that person (i.e., earliest date on which the person first has both conditions present in 2020).
   3.2 Person-level distinctness: Cohort count should be the number of distinct persons meeting the criteria.

4. Visit/setting
   4.1 No restriction on care setting: Qualifying condition occurrences may be recorded in any care setting (inpatient, outpatient, emergency, primary care, etc.).
   4.2 No requirement for same encounter: The influenza and constipation occurrences do not need to be on the same encounter or same visit, only both must occur in 2020 for the same person.

5. Time window
   5.1 Study time window: All qualifying events must occur within the 2020 calendar year (2020-01-01 through 2020-12-31 inclusive).
   5.2 Index date determination reiterated: Index date = date of the later of the two qualifying condition occurrences within this 2020 window.

6. Exclusions
   6.1 No additional clinical exclusions: Do not exclude persons for prior history of either condition outside 2020, nor exclude for missing other demographic data, unless the data necessary to evaluate sex or age are missing (see Assumptions).
   6.2 No visit-type exclusions.

7. Exit
   7.1 Cohort exit date: Each person exits the cohort on the index date (i.e., cohort era length = 0 days). This collection is intended for a cross-sectional/count metric on that index date.

8. Assumptions (explicit, conservative defaults)
   8.1 Condition concept sets: “Influenza” is any condition concept that represents influenza (all acute influenza SNOMED/ICD concepts and their descendants). “Constipation” is any condition concept that represents constipation (and descendants). Implementation in ATLAS should include appropriate standard concept(s) and descendants for each clinical concept. If multiple related subtypes exist (e.g., influenza A/B), include all influenza subtypes.
   8.2 Age calculation: Age is computed using the person’s birth date and the index date using full date precision. If only year of birth is available in the source, compute age conservatively using (index year - birth year) and include patients if the result falls between 20 and 25 inclusive. If birth date is missing such that age cannot be determined, exclude the person (Assumption: require determinable age).
   8.3 Sex definition: “Male” is defined by the recorded sex concept indicating male. If sex is missing or recorded as unknown, exclude the person (Assumption: require determinable recorded sex).
   8.4 Event timing: Only condition occurrences with event dates within 2020-01-01 to 2020-12-31 are allowed to qualify. Condition occurrences before or after 2020 do not satisfy the requirement for that condition.
   8.5 Multiple events: If a person has multiple occurrences of influenza and/or constipation in 2020, use dates as described to determine the index date (the later of one influenza and one constipation event). For per-person deduplication, use the earliest such index date in 2020.
   8.6 Observation continuity: Continuous observation time is not required. Persons without continuous observation are eligible provided qualifying events and demographic data are present in the data.

9. Output/metric
   9.1 Metric requested: Provide the patient count (number of unique persons) meeting the cohort definition above in 2020."}
